title: Haunted for 40 years: Bridgwater author shares paranormal experiences
excerpt: Robbert Turner is set to share decades of personal haunting and paranormal experiences that even led him to seek an exorcism
content:
A Bridgwater author and 'psychic medium' is preparing to share what he describes as forty years of paranormal experiences during an upcoming talk at Bridgwater Library.

Robbert Turner, who has lived in Bridgwater for the past 16 years, will present a free talk about his book, Help! Love, Karen: Diary of a Poltergeist, on October 2.

The book documents what Turner says were years of unexplained events centred around a mysterious figure haunting him called "Karen", whose story he claims gradually unfolded through a series of unusual incidents over the past decades.

Speaking to the Bridgwater Mercury, Robbert says his interest in the paranormal stretches back to childhood.

He said his earliest haunting experience came when he was five years old and woke abruptly feeling "a nail being embedded" in his toe, an event that left him convinced there was "more to this world than meets the physical eye".

After working for many years as a regional press photographer in East Devon, Turner spent time in Los Angeles, where he says a growing interest in spirituality developed further following encounters with psychic mediums in both Britain and the United States.

The events detailed in his book began, he says, during a visit to his brother's home in Cornwall in 1986.

Robbert, recalls being left alone in the house when what he describes as a series of unexplained occurrences began.

He said: "All the lights suddenly went off and the television started to change its channels rapidly before switching itself off.

"A disturbing message in the greasy film of my bedroom mirror. ‘HELP’."

He added: "This started a rapidly increasing trail of inexplicable phenomena which turned into a slowly unveiling as to who was behind everything."

The cover for Robbert's book, based on the description of the girl he says he's seen (Image: Robbert Turner)

Over the next days, Robbert claims the recurring figure began to reveal itself as Karen, a young girl who had died decades ago.

Robbert said he carefully documented the subsequent events as they happened: "As soon as something happened, I wrote it down. Time, date, whatever. It was good because I wouldn't remember all the incidents."

Among the strangest moments described in the book are messages allegedly appearing on a typewriter, missing keys being discovered in a graveyard, and red-headed matchsticks repeatedly turning up in unexpected places - including jammed inside a toothpaste tube.

While Robbert believes the experiences were paranormal in nature, he acknowledges that others may reach different conclusions.

What is certain, he says, is the impact the events had on his life.

"It pushed me to the edge," he said. "I could feel myself cracking under the strain of it all because it was relentless."

"The loss of personal control over your whole environment, and it was not only affecting [me], but friends and family."

Robbert says the haunting became so extreme he even had an exorcism performed for his protection.

In the years since Karen's dramatic first appearance, Robbert says he's developed his skills as a psychic medium, and sought to understand more about his paranormal experiences, and who Karen might have been.

He said: “We don’t like to be frightened, do we? But as far as I was concerned, I was determined to get to the bottom of the whole thing and put it to rest.”

The free talk will take place at Bridgwater Library from 2pm to 3.30pm on Friday, October 2.

Places are limited and advance booking is required via emailing brwlib@somerset.gov.uk or speaking to a member of library staff.
